title: Reverse Engineering
summary: Read a compiled program you built yourself: parse the file, decode the instructions, lift them to pseudocode, record evidence, and prove a rebuild equal, then learn the field around that pipeline with its main tools.

prerequisites.title: Python, hexadecimal, and the command line
prerequisites.description: You can read Python, run a command, and convert between hexadecimal and decimal. No prior assembly or binary analysis experience is required.

prerequisites.title: Python 3.10 or later
prerequisites.description: Every reader, decoder, lifter, and ledger in the path uses the Python standard library only. The compiled fixtures are in the repository.

prerequisites.title: clang for rebuilding fixtures and Lesson 36
prerequisites.description: clang rebuilds the fixtures from source and compiles the Lesson 36 differential driver. Without it, Lesson 36 reads the committed objects and reports its behaviour claims as unknown.

prerequisites.title: Analyze only programs you built or are authorized to analyze
prerequisites.description: Before Lesson 32's lab, confirm that every target is a program you wrote and compiled, or one with written authorization. Lesson 32 opens with the law and the authorization rules.

invocation.portableFallback: Use learn-reverse-engineering to start or resume the Reverse Engineering path.

conceptualFallback: Read the website or each lesson's docs/en.md and trace the named fixture by hand. Record the checkpoint as conceptual and leave decoder, lifter, ledger, and proof evidence pending until the repository and Python 3 are available.

quickStart.goal: Parse one compiled object you did not hand-write the bytes of, and name its sections, symbols, and relocations.
expectedEvidence: The reader names the file format from its first four bytes.
The section table, the four function symbols, and the relocation records print with their offsets.

lessons.title: Program Anatomy: An ELF Reader From Scratch
lessons.checkpoint: Parse an ELF64 and a Mach-O fixture, and match the section, symbol, and relocation output against the recorded reference.

lessons.title: Disassembly and Control Flow: From Bytes to a Graph You Can Check
lessons.checkpoint: Decode the fixture functions with a result that matches llvm-objdump, then build the control-flow graph and its dominators for grade.

lessons.title: Lifting to Pseudocode: IR, SSA, and Structuring From Scratch
lessons.checkpoint: Lift percent_change to SSA and structured pseudocode, and explain each difference from the Ghidra output.

lessons.title: Evidence, Confidence, and Unknowns in Binary Analysis
lessons.checkpoint: Record one finding as an evidence entry with its confidence, limitations, and residual unknowns, and recompute its evidence id.

lessons.title: Rebuild and Prove Equal: Differential Tests, Byte Comparison, and the Evidence Loop
lessons.checkpoint: Run the differential grid and the relocation-masked byte comparison on a rebuilt function, and record the result as evidence.

lessons.title: The Reverse Engineering Landscape: History, Tool Families, and How a Decompiler Is Built
lessons.checkpoint: Run the comparison harness on the four fixture functions and explain each place where a tool invents or misses code, then name the same pipeline stage in three tools.

lessons.title: Calling Conventions and Stack Frames: System V, Windows x64, and AArch64
lessons.checkpoint: Infer parameter count, frame size, and saved registers for one function under three ABIs, and cite the spec rule behind each inference.

lessons.title: Compiler Idioms: What Optimization Does to Your Code and How to Read It Back
lessons.checkpoint: Recover a divisor from its magic multiplier and shift, and classify the switch lowering of one function at -O0 and -O2 with the evidence instructions.

lessons.title: Linking, Loading, and Stripped Binaries: PLT, GOT, Imports, Fixups, and Function Identification
lessons.checkpoint: Trace one imported call through its stub and fixup in a Mach-O build, and name the functions of a stripped build with signatures made from the unstripped one.

lessons.title: Recovering Data and Types: Structs, Arrays, C++ Objects, and DWARF
lessons.checkpoint: Infer a struct layout from memory accesses and match every field against the DWARF reader, then resolve one virtual call to its vtable slot.

lessons.title: Dynamic Analysis of Your Own Program: Debuggers, Traces, and Confirming Static Claims
lessons.checkpoint: Grade the static claims for one build as confirmed, refuted, or not observed from a debugger transcript, and explain the -O2 build where breakpoints never hit.

lessons.title: Beyond Native Code: Python, JVM, .NET, and WebAssembly Bytecode
lessons.checkpoint: Parse the same function from a .pyc, a class file, and a Wasm module, match each listing against the reference tool, and list what each container keeps.

lessons.title: Binary Diffing and Symbolic Execution: Matching Functions and Solving for Inputs
lessons.checkpoint: Match functions between two optimization levels with the staged matcher, show the relocation case that masking fixes, and solve one input for each path of grade.

lessons.title: AI-Assisted Reverse Engineering: LLM Decompilers, Analysis Agents, and Ground Truth
lessons.checkpoint: Score the candidate reconstructions on all six scorecard fields and explain the failing evidence for each candidate that does not pass.
